extracted.intended_audience: students and researchers (ML/NLP) building paper-reviewer recommendation / conference assignment systems
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating automated systems that recommend the best k reviewers for a given (unseen) paper using topic models, collaborative filtering, matrix factorization, and citation/section-based signals. The report documents datasets, preprocessing, algorithms, evaluation (RMSE/10-fold CV), and practical issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem formulation: recommend top-k reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a paper and a list of available reviewers, recommend the reviewers best suited for reviewing the given paper; formally, given a set of N reviewers, find the subset of best k reviewers for a given 'unseen' paper using the available resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the canonical task definition that guides dataset construction, model output, and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption on paper format and sections
rubrics_metrics.description: The work assumes papers have a format close to the NIPS format and each paper has an explicit Experiment Section or a Related works section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach can be applied generally with slight algorithm modifications, but some methods (section extraction, weighting) rely on identifiable sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent papers and reviewers with topic vectors (LDA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent papers as vectors of topics obtained from an LDA model trained on a scientific corpus; represent a reviewer as the average vector comprising all his/her paper vectors (author profile = average of authored paper vectors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as initial paper/reviewer vectors (ui, vj) for downstream methods and as a baseline (TPMS-like).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hybrid collaborative filtering (user+item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use both user-based and item-based collaborative filtering to fill the incomplete reviewer-paper relevance matrix; compute user-based and item-based relevance scores and take their average.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update formulas provided (with ρuser, ρitem weighting); relies on similarity metrics between reviewers and between papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Similarity metrics to compute vector similarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Use cosine, Jaccard, and Pearson similarity metrics to compute similarity between any two vectors (reviewer-reviewer or paper-paper).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulas given; use cross-validation to select the best metric for predictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of initial fill value for unfilled entries in CF
rubrics_metrics.description: Set an initial value (reported as 1.0) to each unfilled entry in the relevance matrix before running collaborative filtering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initialization affects CF behavior; the system uses all three similarity metrics and picks the best via cross-validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metric: RMSE with 10-fold cross-validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate predicted relevance scores against ground truth using Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) computed by 10-fold cross validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divide actual relevance scores into 10 parts, train on 9 parts and compute RMSE on the held-out part; relevance scores range from 0 to 3 (Very Relevant=3, Relevant=2, Slightly Relevant=1, Irrelevant=0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem with BoW/LDA semantic richness (TPMS limitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: LDA or BoW topic modelling used by TPMS is not semantically rich enough; substituting with richer embeddings (e.g., Word2Vec) can improve results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motivates exploring vector-based sentence/paper embeddings rather than purely topic counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sections should be weighted differently for reviewer assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Not all sections of the paper are equally important; Related Works and Experiment/Results sections often yield more useful topics for reviewer assignment and should be given higher weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose clustering sentences and assigning priority weights to clusters; use weights to boost relevance scores for cited authors or boost topic frequencies for high-priority clusters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence clustering + priority weighting
rubrics_metrics.description: Cluster all sentences in the paper and assign priority weights to clusters to identify important sections/topics for reviewer assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weights can be used (1) to boost the relevance score of cited persons if available in the reviewer list, and (2) to boost topic frequency whose sentences lie in higher-priority clusters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sent2Vec (vector averaging) for sentence embeddings and its limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute a sentence vector as the average of word vectors (S = sum wi / n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Averaging causes loss of information (example: two-word sentence with vectors -1 and +1 averages to 0), leading to poor clustering; observe large central cluster and high merger distances in agglomerative clustering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bag-of-vectors sentence similarity (pairwise word cosines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute sentence similarity by summing cosines of all word vector pairs between two sentences and build an affinity matrix for spectral clustering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After removing stop words, form all (ui,vj) pairs and compute normalized sum of dot-products to obtain sentence similarity; apply spectral clustering to this affinity matrix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternating optimization to jointly optimize relevance matrix and vectors
rubrics_metrics.description: Hypothesize that initial LDA vectors are suboptimal; alternate between (1) optimizing the reviewer-paper relevance matrix given current paper and reviewer vectors and (2) using matrix factorization to obtain optimal paper and reviewer vectors from the matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initialize ui, vj to LDA vectors; repeat updates (they implemented 5 epochs) to refine both matrix and vectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-rank matrix factorization with SGD
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor the reviewer-paper relevance matrix into paper and reviewer matrices using low-rank matrix factorization optimized with stochastic gradient descent (SGD), minimizing squared error plus L2 regularization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective and SGD update rules provided; used 5000 iterations, step length 0.0002, λ = 0.02 in experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularize factorization to stay close to initial LDA vectors
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify the matrix factorization objective to penalize deviation of learned vectors from initial LDA vectors (add terms ||ui − ui*||^2 and ||vi − vi*||^2), ensuring document topics keep influence on relevance scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change enforces the paper and reviewer vectors not to deviate too much from the LDA vectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model cited authors as high-relevance reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of papers cited in the Experiments or Related Works sections are likely good reviewers; if cited authors are in the reviewer list assign them high relevance; if not, compute their author profiles and add them as new reviewer rows with high scores for the cited paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completing the matrix with these added rows increases relevance scores of reviewers similar to the cited authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprocessing standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard NLP preprocessing used: Porter stemming, stop-word removal, manual extracting of Experiment section (due to diverse section titles), extracting references via bibtex files, and creating author profiles as the average of an author's paper vectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These preprocessing steps are necessary to create consistent inputs for LDA/embeddings and for identifying cited authors and experiment sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset composition and ground-truth relevance labels
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation dataset should include abstracts/papers, a reviewer list, and paper-reviewer relevance judgments; example dataset used: 148 NIPS 2006 papers, 364 reviewers, 650 relevance judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground truth relevance used: Very Relevant=3, Relevant=2, Slightly Relevant=1, Irrelevant=0. Using reviewer feedback and reviewer ratings from conference websites can serve as training/validation signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation hyperparameter choices (example settings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical parameter settings used in experiments: LDA with unigrams, 127 topics, 5 passes, minimum probability 0; Alternating Optimization run for 5 epochs; matrix factorization 5000 iterations, step length 0.0002, λ = 0.02.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are example settings; hyperparameter tuning (hypertuning) is suggested in future work for improved performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of similarity metric by cross-validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use cross-validation accuracy (RMSE) to choose which similarity metric (cosine, Jaccard, Pearson) yields best predictions for collaborative filtering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train CF using all metrics and select the best according to CV; reported RMSE comparisons for cosine/jaccard/pearson in experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical challenges that affect system quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of dataset scarcity/confidentiality for reviewer-paper assignments, partial/non-portable code availability, and author name-disambiguation issues when extracting cited author profiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors limit reproducibility and evaluation; solutions include requesting datasets from authors, robust name disambiguation, and advocating for open-sourcing code/data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended future extensions as quality criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested improvements include hypertuning methods, using full papers instead of abstracts to construct profiles, finding important sections independent of relevance scores, extending to papers without clear experiment/related-work sections, and pursuing citation-graph-based matching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These directions indicate criteria to improve coverage, robustness, and semantic fidelity of reviewer recommendation systems.
